name: add respects the capacity and keeps the newest state
input: three additions to a capacity-two buffer
test:
import random
random.seed(7)
buffer = ReplayBuffer(2)
buffer.add('s0', 'a0', 0.0, 's1', False)
buffer.add('s1', 'a1', 1.0, 's2', False)
buffer.add('s2', 'a2', 2.0, 's3', True)
assert len(buffer.buffer) == 2
assert 's2' in {item['state'] for item in buffer.buffer}
assert all(item['sample_count'] == 0 for item in buffer.buffer)
assert buffer.get_last_state() == 's2'

name: add_batch preserves transition fields and behaves like ordered adds
test:
buffer = ReplayBuffer(4)
buffer.add_batch(
    ['s0', 's1'],
    ['left', 'right'],
    [0.25, 0.75],
    ['s1', 's2'],
    [False, True],
)
assert buffer.buffer == [
    {'state': 's0', 'action': 'left', 'reward': 0.25, 'next_state': 's1', 'done': False, 'sample_count': 0},
    {'state': 's1', 'action': 'right', 'reward': 0.75, 'next_state': 's2', 'done': True, 'sample_count': 0},
]
assert buffer.get_last_state() == 's1'

name: sample persists counts and evicts exactly at the limit
input: sample the only stored transition twice
test:
buffer = ReplayBuffer(1)
transition = ('s0', 'act', 1.5, 's1', False)
buffer.add(*transition)
assert buffer.sample() == transition
assert len(buffer.buffer) == 1
assert buffer.buffer[0]['sample_count'] == 1
assert buffer.sample() == transition
assert buffer.buffer == []
assert buffer.get_last_state() == 's0'

name: overflowing add_batch remains bounded
input: a four-item batch added to capacity two
test:
import random
random.seed(11)
buffer = ReplayBuffer(2)
buffer.add_batch(
    ['s0', 's1', 's2', 's3'],
    [0, 1, 2, 3],
    [0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
    ['s1', 's2', 's3', 's4'],
    [False, False, False, True],
)
assert len(buffer.buffer) == 2
assert 's3' in {item['state'] for item in buffer.buffer}
assert buffer.get_last_state() == 's3'
